as_told.title: Questions to the Nine about Russian guerrilla code names

plain: The claim is that in the 1970s, at a private research lab called Lab Nine in Ossining, New York, run by a scientist named Andrija Puharich, sessions were taped in which people tried remote viewing, meaning describing distant places or secrets with the mind alone, and some targets were military ones. A researcher named Greg Malatzi tells Michels that some tapes ask things like what time is best to remote view "the Kremlin so we can get into it." A second researcher on the same episode, who is not named, describes the tapes the same way but gives a different example. In his version the question is what code name Russian guerrilla soldiers are using. Neither names a source beyond the tapes themselves. They bring it up because, if true, a private lab's mind-reading sessions were being aimed at Cold War intelligence targets.
